title: Split-coordinate ideal becomes principal at fibre-generic chart primes
statement:
Let $R\to B$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Suppose $B\otimes_R E$ is an integral domain for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and every field extension $E/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Fix $R$-linear maps $i:B\to F=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in A}R$ and $\rho:F\to B$ with $\rho i=1_B$. Let $J=(j_1,\ldots,j_t)\subset B$, and let $C\subset R$ be generated by the coordinates of $i(j_1),\ldots,i(j_t)$. Let $h\in R$, set $I=hC$, and choose $a\in I$ and $c\in C$ with $a=hc$. Put $R^*=R[I/a]\subset R[1/a]$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] and $B^*=B\otimes_RR^*$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. Then $B^*$ is flat over $R^*$, multiplication by each of $a,h,c$ is injective on both $R^*$ and $B^*$, and $CR^*=cR^*$. The natural localization identifies $(R^*)_a$ with $R_a$, and $h$ is invertible there with inverse $c/a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. For every prime $\mathfrak p^*\subset R^*$, the fibre $B^*\otimes_{R^*}\kappa(\mathfrak p^*)$ is an integral domain, the natural map
$$ B^*/\mathfrak p^*B^*\longrightarrow B^*\otimes_{R^*}\kappa(\mathfrak p^*) $$
is injective, $\mathfrak q^*=\mathfrak p^*B^*$ is prime, and $JB^*_{\mathfrak q^*}=cB^*_{\mathfrak q^*}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text: By [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], $R^*$ is a subring of $R_a$. The images of $a,h,c$ are units in $R_a$, since $a=hc$; hence multiplication by each is injective on its subring $R^*$. Localization of the inclusion gives an injective map $(R^*)_a\to R_a$: if $x/a^n$ maps to zero, then $x=0$ already in $R^*$. It is surjective because its image contains $R$ and $1/a$. Thus $(R^*)_a=R_a$, and $h(c/a)=1$ there. These fraction computations also cover $R_a=0$, with injectivity on the zero module understood literally.

proof.text: For every $d\in C$ put $e_d=hd/a\in R^*$, since $hd\in I$. In $R_a$ one has $ce_d=d$, hence the same equality holds in $R^*$. Therefore $CR^*\subset cR^*$, and the reverse inclusion follows from $c\in C$. This proves $CR^*=cR^*$ directly, without invoking a principalization theorem.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p^*\subset R^*$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be its inverse image in $R$, a prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] the residue fields of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ at $\mathfrak p$ and of $\operatorname{Spec}R^*$ at $\mathfrak p^*$ [def-weil-residue-field] are $R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ and $R^*_{\mathfrak p^*}/\mathfrak p^*R^*_{\mathfrak p^*}$, compatibly with the maps from $R$ and $R^*$. The composite $R\to R^*\to\kappa(\mathfrak p^*)$ kills $\mathfrak p$ and sends $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ to units, so by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra](d) it factors through a field homomorphism $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p^*)$. Thus $E=\kappa(\mathfrak p^*)$ is a field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ whose $R$-algebra structure is the one through $R^*$. The maps $(b\otimes r)\otimes e\mapsto b\otimes re$ and $b\otimes e\mapsto(b\otimes1)\otimes e$ are inverse ring maps between $B^*\otimes_{R^*}E$ and $B\otimes_RE$; their well-definedness and inverse equations are the tensor balancing relations. The latter ring is an integral domain by the hypothesis, so the former is an integral domain.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, fibre hypothesis after chart base change

proof.text: Set $D=R^*/\mathfrak p^*$ and $M=B^*/\mathfrak p^*B^*$. The quotient $D$ is a domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-quotient-flat] applied to step 3, $M$ is flat over $D$; [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain] makes multiplication by every nonzero element of $D$ injective on $M$. Let $U$ be the image of $R^*\setminus\mathfrak p^*$ in $B^*$; it acts on $M$ through the nonzero elements of $D$. The fraction map $M\to U^{-1}M$ is therefore injective: $m/1=0$ implies $um=0$ for some $u\in U$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], hence $m=0$. By step 6 and [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra](b), $\kappa(\mathfrak p^*)$ is the fraction field $(R^*\setminus\mathfrak p^*)^{-1}(R^*/\mathfrak p^*)$ of $D$. So [lem-trf-fibre-module-localization], applied to $R^*\to B^*$, the prime $\mathfrak p^*$ and $N=B^*$, gives the isomorphism $B^*\otimes_{R^*}\kappa(\mathfrak p^*)\cong U^{-1}M$ whose inverse sends $[b]/s$ to $b\otimes(1/s)$; on $s=1$ it is the natural map $[b]\mapsto b\otimes1$. Thus the natural map from $M$ to the fibre is injective. The fibre is a nonzero integral domain by step 6 and $M\to$ fibre is a unital ring map, so $M$ is a nonzero integral domain and $\mathfrak q^*=\mathfrak p^*B^*$ is prime.
